Definition: the arm (as stretched out), or (of animals) the foreleg; figuratively, force
BiblicalUsage: The arm is the Bible's picture of strength, and most often it is God's arm. With a stretched-out arm He brought Israel out of Egypt, and the prophets look for that arm again — bared before the nations, revealed in the Servant, carrying the lambs close. Human arms break and fail; the arm of the LORD does not. It saves, it rules, and it gathers.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the arm of the LORD is not a figure of speech for power in general but a promise about who does the saving. No human arm carried Israel out, and no human arm carries me now. My position is that when Scripture says His arm is not shortened, it means exactly that: the strength that saved then is the strength that saves still.
